purpose: Tbo-filgrastim helps your body make more white blood cells, which are the cells that fight infection. It is mainly used to lower the risk of infection in people who are receiving chemotherapy for cancer. By boosting your white blood cell count, it helps keep you safer during cancer treatment.
how_it_works: Your bone marrow is like a factory that makes blood cells. Chemotherapy can slow down that factory, leaving you with too few white blood cells to fight off germs. Tbo-filgrastim acts like a signal that tells your bone marrow to speed up and produce more white blood cells quickly.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bone or muscle aching, especially in your back, hips, or legs — this happens because your bone marrow is working extra hard. You might also notice redness, swelling, or bruising at the injection site. Some people feel tired or have a mild fever.
warnings: Rarely, this medicine can cause a serious condition called spleen rupture, where the spleen can enlarge and burst — call your doctor right away if you have sudden, severe pain in your upper left belly or shoulder. It can also cause serious lung problems (breathing difficulty, fever), allergic reactions, or inflammation of the tiny air sacs in the lungs. Let your doctor know all your medical history before starting this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 5 micrograms per kilogram of body weight, given as a shot under the skin (injection) once a day. It is usually started the day after chemotherapy and continued until your white blood cell count recovers. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give the injection at home if needed.
